A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRASS research framework, despite the changed title and substantive revisions. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRASS results on eight benchmark datasets, ZINC ablations, stochastic-output variance measurements, and computational timings in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original GRASS results on nine benchmark datasets, expanded ZINC and PascalVOC-SP ablations, stochastic-output variance measurements, and computational and storage results.

M1.justification: Section 3 introduces D-RRWP, a truncated-eigendecomposition alternative to exact RRWP. It also concatenates forward and reverse RRWP edge encodings, replaces PN-V with batch normalization, removes degree-scaled attention, and includes the receiving node in attention neighborhoods. These change preprocessing and layer computations. Edge flipping and random edge removal were already present.

E1.justification: All eight original benchmark datasets remain, and v3 adds COCO-SP evaluation in Table 2. This extends the existing superpixel node-classification coverage to another image corpus. The new PascalVOC-SP ablations use a dataset already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add NeuralWalker, while Table 2 removes GatedGCN+RWSE. More substantially, v3 adds direct component comparisons against GAT, GatedGCN, and Transformer attention, plus LapPE encoding alternatives, in Tables 4 and 6. These substantially expand the comparisons testing the proposed components.

E3.justification: Retained benchmark settings change: CLUSTER training decreases from 100 to 50 epochs, PascalVOC-SP from 600 to 500, and PATTERN/CLUSTER rewiring degree from 15 to 6. Their edge-removal rates increase from 0.3 to 0.5. New ablations introduce parameter-budget matching, padded LapPE controls, and optimization adjustments. Table 2 also adopts externally retuned LRGB baseline configurations.

E4.justification: v1 provides ZINC component-removal ablations and a regular-graph degree sweep. v3 substantially expands these into encoding and attention replacement studies, regular versus non-regular rewiring, fully connected controls, optimizer replacement, and corresponding PascalVOC-SP analyses. Tables 3–6 additionally examine runtime, peak memory, and D-RRWP storage requirements.

E5.justification: Table 1 raises reported training-run counts from 8 to 16 for ZINC and from 6 to 8 for other GNN benchmarks. ZINC rewiring-variance estimation changes from 30 to 100 test evaluations, and Figure 4 adds standard-error bars. Mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remains, but v1's four-run preprocessing-time uncertainty is omitted in v3.

E6.justification: Numerous results are replaced under revised models and settings: ZINC MAE changes from 0.046 to 0.047, CIFAR10 accuracy from 82.471 to 83.750, and PATTERN accuracy from 90.997 to 89.177. COCO-SP MacroF1 of 0.4752 and extensive ablation/resource results are added. These are not controlled version-to-version gains. v3's claimed fifth-place Peptides-func ranking conflicts with Table 2, which lists eleven higher means.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds the D-RRWP derivation: a symmetric normalized transition matrix, truncated eigenpairs, approximate matrix powers, time/storage bounds, and an argument for setting walk length equal to the number of eigenpairs. The earlier random-regular-graph arguments largely move to Appendix A.1; the diameter bound is additionally qualified as asymptotic and applying to almost every such graph.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on random rewiring, graph-tailored attention, and the connection between message passing and sparse Transformers. v3 adds a novel efficient encoding contribution, D-RRWP, and makes the combination of encoding, rewiring, and attention central in the abstract and conclusion. The broad state-of-the-art performance claim remains.

C2.justification: v1 partly attributes performance to narrow, deep models and inductive bias on small datasets. v3 instead develops component-specific interpretations concerning D-RRWP efficiency, regular rewiring, attention alternatives, and the limited influence of minor design choices. Section 5.1 newly acknowledges that scalability on extremely large graphs has not been thoroughly evaluated; the nondeterministic-output limitation remains.

D1.justification: Both versions already provide detailed hyperparameter and timing tables. v3 updates encoding, hardware, compilation, and checkpointing information; discloses PyTorch Geometric implementations and ablation adjustments; and corrects pseudocode loop endpoints. It omits explicit 1cycle schedule naming and RAM/VRAM capacity rows. Both versions still promise a future GitHub release without providing access.

R1.justification: The core relationship to RRWP/GRIT, GPS, Exphormer, and BigBird remains. v3 more explicitly credits existing random rewiring and locates novelty in the component combination and D-RRWP. It adds NeuralWalker, the LRGB reassessment, and decomposition/implementation references while pruning earlier background citations. The extensive prose rewrite exceeds the change in underlying research positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and related-work section are extensively rewritten, and GRASS's expanded name changes. Methods explanations are reorganized, random-rewiring theory moves into Appendix A, and experiments gain separate benchmarking and ablation subsections. The conclusion gains dedicated limitations and reproducibility subsections, and the appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: The architecture overview is redrawn and moved from the appendix into the main text. v3 adds a simplified attention diagram and an ablation chart, updates the detailed attention diagram, and substantially restructures ablation tables to display controls and resource costs. Benchmark tables gain comparator rows and a COCO-SP column, while appendix tables are regrouped.

improvement.justification: v1 claims advantages for graph-tailored attention but provides only limited component ablations on ZINC. v3's alternative-attention, encoding, and rewiring comparisons on ZINC and PascalVOC-SP substantially strengthen evidence for its design choices. D-RRWP gains mathematical explanation and an empirical storage/accuracy comparison, and stronger LRGB baselines improve evaluation credibility. Explicitly acknowledging untested large-graph scalability also improves qualification of the claims. These gains outweigh the incorrect Peptides-func ranking and loss of preprocessing-time uncertainty reporting.
